business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Distribution of Virgin Polyethylene and Polypropylene Granules

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (unitary jurisdiction; no separate sub-state fiscal regime)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - English Common Law, Samoan statute, and customary law (fa'a Samoa)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand, Norway, the Netherlands and other G20 partners
PACER-Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus)
WTO Membership (GATT, GATS, Trade Facilitation Agreement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations 2009; International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended (registered office, registers of members/directors, beneficial ownership record-keeping, bearer share prohibition); International Trusts Act 1987 (as relevant); Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Guidelines; directives issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO records maintained at the Samoan registered office through a licensed registered agent and produced to the Registrar, FIU and law enforcement on lawful demand; not open to public search)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the bio-data page of the valid passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner, notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or notarized bank reference letter for each UBO and any corporate shareholder, issued within 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed financial institution / notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address for each UBO (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months), notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank; notarized by a competent notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of any non-resident corporate shareholder, issued within 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or corporate service provider in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Executed KYC/UBO due diligence questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration signed by each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoa registered agent (execution by UBO/director) / notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories and counterparty banks against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list and the domestic list maintained by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; at least two independent screening engines must be used. PEP status triggers Enhanced Due Diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Documents originating from states not party to the Hague Apostille Convention must be authenticated by full consular legalization through the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade before acceptance. Unverified disclosures block incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - International Companies Registry, Apia; name clearance applications are lodged exclusively through licensed Samoa registered agents under the International Companies Act 1987
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the operative registry language. The proposed name must use Latin characters; any name in Samoan (Gagana Samoa) or another language requires a certified English transliteration/translation. The statutory suffix 'Limited' or abbreviation 'Ltd.' is mandatory unless exempted by the Registrar.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens implying royal or government connection: 'Government', 'Crown', 'Ministry', 'State', 'Samoa'
Regulated financial tokens requiring prior ministerial approval: 'Bank', 'Banking', 'Trust', 'Trustee', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Reinsurance', 'Fund'
Professional and educational tokens: 'University', 'Polytechnic', 'Chamber of Commerce', 'Institute'
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoan or foreign listed company or reserved name
Obscene, offensive, unlawful or misleading tokens
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: the licensed registered agent may file a written renewal before expiry; the Registrar may grant one 30-day extension on payment of the prescribed fee. Rejection: written grounds are issued by the Registrar; the applicant may file an administrative appeal through the registered agent within 14 days, supported by submissions and any requisite consents for sensitive tokens. A final refusal may be challenged before the Supreme Court of Samoa by judicial review. Reservation fees are non-refundable and a fresh application must be filed after final refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible to satisfy the statutory registered office requirement: the International Companies Act 1987 mandates a physical registered office in Samoa and a licensed registered agent at all times. A virtual or mail-forwarding address serves only as a supplementary administrative facility. For a medium-risk ISIC 4669 wholesale petrochemical trader, the registered agent will require demonstrable commercial substance (board records, accounting records, UBO files, named local representatives) to prevent shell-type characterization and to satisfy AML/CFT obligations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 15-25% per annum. SIFA and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit conduct unannounced, risk-based inspections of licensed registered agents and may examine customer files; a physical inspection may occur within an AML/CFT examination or commercial substance review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government name reservation and search certificate fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - International Companies Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies Act 1987 (Fees Regulations)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation and registration fee (International Company, nominal capital USD 1,000,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies Act 1987 (Fees Regulations)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent service retainer (Year 1, statutory requirement)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 7–24 (incorporation and constitution), s. 31 (registered office), s. 45 (share capital), ss. 58–71 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing of the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitution) and required statutory notices
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. An International Company may issue shares with par value in any currency; capital may be subscribed and unpaid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association of the Company are hereby appointed as the first directors. RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscription of 1 ordinary share at US$1.00 is approved, ratified, and recorded. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be established in Apia, Samoa, at the office of the registered agent, and that address be used for all statutory communications. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors appointed herein are authorized to open and operate bank accounts, execute trade and payment documentation, and engage service providers. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Company Secretary is appointed and authorized to file all requisite returns and maintain statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Companies Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written or online name clearance application to SIFA stating the proposed corporate name. SIFA conducts an availability search against the International Companies Register. Upon approval, the name is reserved for a period of 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or reserved for another entity, the applicant may file a written appeal with SIFA or immediately submit alternative names for re-clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, including the intended objects, permitted share capital, registered office location, and officer appointment provisions. The registered agent confirms the first director and secretary candidates and obtains consent for appointment.
required_dossiers: Drafted Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act as first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any constitutional provision, the registered agent amends the draft and resubmits the corrected document with a written explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Memorandum and Articles, statutory declarations, and incorporation application through the SIFA-approved registered agent. The Registrar reviews the dossier and, upon satisfaction, issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent forms of directors and secretary
Certified passport copies of shareholders and officers
Registered office consent from the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, the applicant must submit a response through the registered agent within 14 days, providing corrected filings or supplementary explanations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue Certificate and Establish Statutory Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent and SIFA Corporate Services Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent then creates the company statutory registers, records the first share allotment, and files the registered office notice.
required_dossiers: Register of shareholders and share allotment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains clerical discrepancies, the registered agent files a correction request with SIFA supported by the original certificate and payment of the rectification fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold First Board Meeting and Authorize Banking Installation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt unanimous written resolutions approving the share allotment, appointing officers, adopting the corporate seal, and authorizing the opening of bank accounts necessary for international trade, including SWIFT LC and irrevocable LC payment facilities.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration for banking KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed bank requires additional due diligence, the directors must provide revised ownership structure declarations, bank references, or enhanced background information within the bank's requested timeframe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Samoa Business Licence (General Trading and Wholesale Distribution)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Conservation Division, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 3: No Full EIA Report or Environmental Registration required for import and wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules without on-site petrochemical processing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure trading operations. If warehousing is maintained, stored polymers must be handled in compliance with the Samoa Waste Management Act 2004 and National Waste Management Strategy; no wastewater, VOC, or atmospheric discharge thresholds are triggered unless melting, reprocessing, or chemical treatment is performed on site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority is required for any commercial warehouse or office premises. Occupational clearance is required under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2008, including structural load inspection, safe egress, fire extinguisher placement, and workplace health clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) — statutory revenue authority established under the Samoa Revenue Authority Act 2013; administered through the SRA Tax Administration System (TAS) digital portal at https://www.sra.gov.ws; responsible for administration of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, the Income Tax Act 2016, and related revenue laws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 does NOT obtain a Samoan TIN or VAGST registration number as part of its offshore formation; its statutory identifier is the certificate of incorporation and company number issued by the Registrar of International Companies within the Samoan International Finance Authority (IFA). Procedure for a foreign-owned IC: (1) instruct a licensed Samoan registered agent / company service provider; (2) file the constitution, Form 1 incorporation application, and a non-residence declaration with the IFA; (3) obtain the certificate of incorporation, tax exemption certificate, and annual license; (4) no step is required before the Samoa Revenue Authority unless the IC later breaches its non-resident status, elects domestic treatment, or carries on taxable activity in Samoa, in which case the IC must apply to the SRA for a TIN using the standard SRA TIN application form supported by the incorporation certificate, directors' register, and registered agent confirmation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — Non-resident International Company; the IC is statutorily exempt under the International Companies Act 1987 from all Samoan taxes, including income tax, VAGST (GST), stamp duty, and exchange control, subject to the territorial limitation that the IC may not carry on business in Samoa, hold Samoan land or Samoan domestic company shares, or transact with Samoan residents except for prescribed administrative services; all wholesale principal-to-principal trading income from the bulk resale of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules is outside Samoa's territorial tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime. Available elections are: (1) the IC may elect in its constitution to adopt or exclude elective provisions of the International Companies Act 1987 (elective provisions mechanism); (2) the IC may elect by special resolution to be re-domiciled or converted into a Samoan domestic company, which prospectively extinguishes the tax-exemption certificate and subjects the entity to full Samoan taxation; (3) hybrid entity treatment is not cognizable in Samoa, so the classification analysis must be performed solely in the jurisdiction of the beneficial owner (e.g., a U.S. owner may check the box to treat the exempt IC as a disregarded entity); (4) the IC may elect its own internal accounting currency but may not elect any Samoan tax regime because no nexus exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST — Value Added Goods and Services Tax (GST) imposed under the Samoa Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 (as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoa Tala) annual taxable turnover threshold for mandatory VAGST registration of any person carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa; an International Company engaged in offshore bulk petrochemical polymer resale has no Samoan taxable activity and therefore no VAGST registration obligation, regardless of global turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not mandate real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital tax stamping; VAGST operates on a self-assessment basis using conventional commercial invoices. The SRA TAS portal supports electronic filing and payment of returns, but no API-based invoice clearance is imposed. For the exempt IC, standard commercial invoices, warehouse transfer documents, and SWIFT/LC records are retained as commercial and beneficial-ownership evidence rather than fiscal invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, exports of goods from Samoa are zero-rated where the goods are physically removed from Samoa and ownership passes to a non-resident recipient within prescribed time limits; offshore services supplied to a non-resident recipient for use wholly outside Samoa are likewise zero-rated. The Samoan International Company does not rely on this VAGST zero-rating mechanism because the virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules never enter Samoan territory: inventory is held at third-country producer warehouses or bonded facilities, title passes on FOB/CIF or similar INCOTERMS at non-Samoan load ports, and the IC's gross margin is realized entirely offshore. Substantiation therefore focuses on proving the exempt non-resident status of the IC through its IFA certificate of tax exemption, invoice flows, warehouse and transportation documentation, and corporate substance records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoan Customs Export Declaration (Cus-Exp Form) — required only if any goods are physically exported from Samoa; typically inapplicable to offshore principal-to-principal polymer resale, but retained where incidental Samoan-origin movements occur
Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill / Air Waybill evidencing the third-country load port, ocean or air carriage, and consignee of the polyethylene and polypropylene granules
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 or MT202 credit advice evidencing settlement of the irrevocable or documentary LC proceeds into the IC's registered foreign-currency bank account
Commercial invoice, packing list, and third-party weight/quality certificates issued at the load port
Underlying master purchase agreements and sale contracts with the polymer producer and downstream buyer, including INCOTERMS, price bases, and title transfer clauses
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a registered VAGST person fraudulently or erroneously claims zero-rating on goods or services that do not qualify, the SRA may assess the full 15% VAGST due, together with late payment penalties and interest under the Tax Administration Act 2016, and may pursue criminal prosecution for fraudulent tax evasion, attracting fines and imprisonment for responsible officers. For the International Company, the IFA and SRA may jointly audit compliance with the non-residence conditions; any breach (e.g., domestic Samoan trading, unauthorized land holding, or sham LC structuring to disguise Samoan-source income) voids the tax-exemption certificate ab initio, exposing the IC to retrospective Samoan income tax and VAGST, civil penalties of up to 100% of the tax shortfall, and striking-off of the company. The principal international clawback risk is mischaracterization of the IC as a permanent establishment in the seller's or buyer's jurisdiction; this is mitigated by maintaining genuine offshore contracts, independent LC payment rails, and economic substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, is the monetary authority and licensed regulator of all authorized dealers in foreign exchange. CBS administers the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Financial Institutions Act 1996, the International Banking Act 1987, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, and holds final authority over foreign-exchange approvals, authorized-dealer licensing, trade-payment clearing rules, and the managed-float policy of the Samoan Tala (WST) against a trade-weighted basket of USD, NZD, EUR and AUD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: WST is a partially convertible, tightly administered currency traded only through CBS-authorized dealers within Samoa. Current-account transactions such as trade settlements, service fees, commissions and dividend remittances receive routine bank-level approval subject to documentary proof and tax-clearance certificates. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections, shareholder-loan disbursements, capital repatriation and portfolio transfers, require individual CBS approval or bank approval within delegated limits, supported by verified corporate records and source-of-funds evidence. Profit remittance by a tax-exempt International Company is lawful but practically gated by the need to demonstrate that no transaction was conducted with Samoan residents, that all underlying trade documents are genuine, and that the beneficial owner is fully identified; otherwise the remittance is treated as a suspect offshore flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and CBS Exchange Control Guidelines, any merchandise physically exported from Samoa must be invoiced in a foreign currency and the exporter must repatriate the full export proceeds to an authorized dealer in Samoa within 30 days from the date of shipment, followed by mandatory surrender and conversion into WST at the prevailing commercial rate, unless a specific CBS retention, offset or exemption is granted. For the WS_IC petrochemical trading entity, goods will normally be drop-shipped from third-country resin producers to end-buyers without entering Samoa, so no Samoan customs export entry or statutory surrender obligation arises on those flows; nevertheless, any third-country receivables credited to a Samoan WST account will be documented by the bank as foreign-currency proceeds subject to source-verification and exchange-control reporting requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_fx_approval_escalation_matr: Authorized dealers may process trade-related outward remittances up to CBS-prescribed per-transaction thresholds with standard supporting documentation; remittances above thresholds, or involving capital-account purposes, must be escalated to CBS on prescribed forms (Outward Remittance/Exchange Control Declaration) with a decision turnaround of 5–10 business days. CBS retains the right to request the complete underlying contract chain, sanctions screening results and proof of arms-length pricing for any bulk-petrochemical settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BSP Samoa Limited (Bank of South Pacific, formerly Westpac Bank Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account – multi-currency WST/USD current account for trade settlement, supplier disbursement and receivables concentration; segregated Capital Escrow Account is not statutorily required for an International Company but may be established as a voluntarily ring-fenced collateral or LC-margin account.

Operational Account – corporate settlement and foreign-currency current account, with documentary trade desks for issuance and advising of Irrevocable Letters of Credit; Capital Escrow Account available on request for trade-finance collateral.
Operational Account – WST domestic current account and limited USD pass-through; generally oriented to domestic retail, public-sector and SME clients rather than offshore trading structures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for use as a primary clearing rail. Samoa has no licensed electronic-money-institution or digital-bank framework, and CBS does not supervise offshore EMIs; therefore the Samoa International Company cannot hold a locally regulated EMI licence and a third-country EMI (e.g., EU, FCA or HKMA-licensed) is treated as an unregulated third-party payment intermediary by Samoan banks. Legal constraints include: (i) funds entering Samoa must pass through a CBS-authorized dealer with complete sender/beneficiary identification and a valid purpose code, which an EMI payment trail rarely satisfies; (ii) exchange-control surrender and reporting obligations become impossible to reconcile if receivables are collected offshore; and (iii) Samoan banks will quarantine or reject inbound transfers from EMI aggregator accounts due to opacity risk. Permissible supporting role: use a regulated EMI solely as a low-value receivables collection point in a fully licensed foreign jurisdiction, immediately onward-settling to the Samoan operational account via direct bank-to-bank MT103, with the EMI never named as the ultimate originator of trade payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Samoan statute mandates physical attendance of directors for account opening; however, commercial-bank policy in practice requires either (i) a physical visit by the ultimate beneficial owner or a senior authorized signatory to the Bank's Apia branch for a compliance interview, or (ii) the vastly slower remote route using notarized and apostilled corporate documents, a live video interview with the relationship manager, and a signed compliance attestation countersigned by the SIFA-licensed registered agent. The remote route typically takes 30–45 business days; the physical route with a pre-booked interview can complete onboarding in 5–10 business days. All Chinese-language corporate documents must be professionally translated into English by an accredited translator and verified by the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company with nominee directors, nominee secretary and no economic substance in Samoa — a classic shell-company red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Charter (memorandum and articles) under the International Companies Act 1987; Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); certified Certificate of Incumbency disclosing directors, secretary and shareholders; nominee service agreements with an SIFA-licensed registered agent; detailed economic-substance declaration and 12-month business plan; apostilled passports and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners; corporate structure chart; accountant's reference letter from a recognized international audit firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Petrochemical wholesale (ISIC 4669 / NAICS 424690) counterparty exposure to OFAC/EU-sanctioned jurisdictions, front companies or opaque transshipment vessels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete upstream and downstream counterparty register with jurisdiction and sanctions screening results; negative confirmation that no Iran, Russia, Venezuela, Democratic People's Republic of Korea or Crimea-linked party is involved; bills of lading, vessel names and IMO numbers, warehouse receipts and customs-clearance records for at least the last 12 months; Incoterms 2020 contract matrix; resin quality certificates and inspection reports; written undertaking to notify the bank of any change in trade route or counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large-volume, rapid in-out settlement with round-tripping characteristics, third-party payment beneficiaries or mismatched invoice narratives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month rolling cash-flow and turnover forecast matching the projected LC cycle; purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists and insurance certificates matched per trade; LC or TT remittance schedule that maps every flow to an identifiable purchase order; source-of-wealth statement for all capital injections; confirmation that no Samoan resident or Samoan company is a counterparty; independent audit trail of margin income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party settlement or funding originating from a digital EMI or a low-regulation jurisdiction, triggering suspicion of unverified wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory licence and authorization of the EMI in its home jurisdiction; six months of consolidated EMI account statements; full KYC/AML file of the ultimate funding party; contractual documentation proving commercial purpose; board resolution authorizing the funding; written commitment to route all future capital via direct bank-to-bank MT103 from the shareholder's regulated bank, bypassing the EMI aggregate account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder contributions must be wired by SWIFT MT103 with an unmistakable purpose narrative: for equity, use 'Shareholder Capital Contribution / Equity Injection', accompanied by a board resolution and the IC's register of shareholders; for borrowings, use 'Shareholder Loan', supported by an executed interest-bearing facility agreement. Under the Exchange Control Act 1976, inward remittances to a CBS-authorized dealer do not require pre-approval when the funds originate from a non-resident regulated bank, the beneficiary is the International Company, and the funds are credited to a foreign-currency account with the remitter name exactly matching the registered shareholder. The onboarding bank will hold the first inward transfer for verification and will require: (i) the registered agent's incumbency certificate; (ii) the directors' resolution authorizing account opening and fund receipt; (iii) the charter and certificate of good standing; and (iv) a sanctions-screen of the remitter. Funds in USD should remain in a USD-denominated operational account to avoid unnecessary WST conversion and re-conversion spreads.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments to third-country resin suppliers will use two complementary rails. First, open-account settlements via SWIFT MT103 from the Samoa USD account, with a narrative containing the supplier's invoice number, trade date, Incoterms rule and vessel or container reference; transactions above the authorized-dealer threshold are escalated to CBS with pro-forma invoice and proof of underlying import. Second, documentary settlements through Irrevocable Documentary Letters of Credit issued or confirmed by BSP Samoa or ANZ Samoa, using MT700/MT707/MT740 messages routed via New York or Sydney correspondent banks, with complying presentation of full bills of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate and independent inspection certificate; given the bulk-polymer margin model, sight LCs are preferred over usance LCs except where a 30–60 day supplier credit to the IC is expressly documented. Standby Letters of Credit (MT760) may be issued for performance security where the buyer requires them. The entity should maintain no less than two fully funded clearing banks to mitigate the correspondent-bank de-risking risk that is present in the Pacific corridor.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (WST/USD and WST/NZD, standard tenors up to 12 months, with genuine trade-exposure documentation)
FX swaps (WST/USD) for short-term liquidity positioning and gap management
Cross-currency swaps for larger trade-finance facilities, subject to CBS case-by-case approval and finfish end-user documentation
OTC FX options (European-style, on a covered back-to-back basis; market participation is thin and requires CBS notification)
FX forwards against NZD and AUD for hedging supplier input costs where procurement is denominated in those currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty per SIFA fee schedule; persistent failure to lodge exposes company to monetary fine and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation annually; no extended calendar billing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% per month or part thereof on the unpaid fee; fees unpaid beyond 3 months after anniversary trigger suspension of Certificate of Good Standing and administrative strike-off by the Registrar

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for a standard International Company; mandatory independent audit applies only to ICs licensed as banks, insurers, or trust businesses; shareholders may trigger a voluntary audit by special resolution
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 1987 requires accounting records sufficient to accurately reflect financial position; no prescribed local GAAP for ICs; IFRS or IFRS for SMEs adopted when a voluntary audit or group reporting is required

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public UBO register for International Companies; the registered agent maintains beneficial ownership records under Samoa AML/CFT obligations; annual KYC and beneficial ownership refresh performed on the incorporation anniversary; share transfers recorded in the Register of Members, with updated UBO details confirmed to the agent within 14 days of any transfer

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable (exempt); voluntary certified audit USD 3,000 - 5,000 if requested

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Company statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 1987; the standard domestic resident corporate income tax headline rate is 27%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 100% permanent exemption for all licensed International Companies: no income tax, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty, no estate duty, no gift duty, and no withholding tax on distributions; the only recurrent government charge is the annual SIFA licence fee calculated on issued share capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return of International Company (Form IC-AR) under the International Companies Act 1987; filed electronically through the SIFA Online e-Filing portal administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); paper filing may be effected through the appointed Samoan Registered Agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return and annual licence fee are due within six months after the International Company's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year IC the deadline is 30 June of each year. No quarterly or monthly income tax returns are required for a tax-exempt International Company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the International Company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the name on the Certificate of Incorporation; English name acceptable; Chinese name may appear as an alias only.
Obtain from the Registered Agent; non-resident directors or shareholders do not require a Samoan resident address.
Must be the office of the licensed Registered Agent; cannot be a P.O. Box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Agent name and licence number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Samoan Registered Agent is the legal point of contact for all government filings and must be retained at all times.
For this entity insert 'Wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules' (ISIC 4669). This field confirms the IC is not trading domestically with Samoan residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital and number of shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare non-resident ownership percentages; bearer shares are prohibited for International Companies in confirmed compliance practice.
Confirm that all shareholders are non-residents of Samoa and that all income will be derived from outside Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Continuance of International Company tax exemption status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick the box accepting the conditions of ICA 1987, Article 124, including the prohibition on carrying on business in Samoa.
IC must indicate whether it is engaged in a relevant activity (distribution and service centre). If yes, provide the SIFA economic substance filing reference.
Calculated from share capital tier; payable by the Registered Agent on behalf of the non-resident owner by 30 June each year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment of the annual licence fee triggers a surcharge of 10% of the licence fee, plus a further penalty of WST 100 per month or part thereof. If the Annual Return and licence fee remain outstanding for three consecutive years, the International Company is automatically struck off and dissolved. Restoration costs include all arrears, a restoration fee of WST 250, and re-registration penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an International Company to any shareholder; Samoa does not impose dividend withholding tax on International Companies by virtue of the International Companies Act 1987 exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No Samoan DTA relief is needed for exempt IC distributions because the domestic statutory rate for International Company dividends is zero. If a foreign tax authority requires evidence of Samoan tax treatment, the beneficial owner must apply to the Ministry of Revenue for a Tax Residency Certificate. The applicant must submit Form MOR-RC, the IC Certificate of Incorporation, the current Annual Return, and a foreign Tax Residency Certificate if a reduced treaty rate is being asserted in the investor's home jurisdiction. Approval is processed administratively within 10 working days where all filings are current.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate for royalties and interest paid by or to an International Company. No Samoan withholding tax applies on cross-border interest or IP royalties derived by an IC. For non-exempt domestic Samoan companies the underlying standard withholding rates are 15% on interest and 15% on royalties, but those rates do not apply to this International Company unless it loses its exempt status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: International Companies engaged in distribution and service centre activity must complete an Economic Substance return where total gross income exceeds WST 3,000,000 per annum. A Samoan Local File will be required where related-party cross-border transactions exceed WST 10,000,000 per annum; a Master File threshold applies at WST 50,000,000 in aggregate covered transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2020 apply. The wholesale distribution of petrochemical polymers is treated as a 'distribution and service centre' relevant activity. The IC must demonstrate: (a) it is managed and controlled in Samoa through board meetings and minutes; (b) it maintains an adequate physical office in Samoa; (c) it employs adequate full-time employees in Samoa; (d) it incurs adequate operating expenditure in Samoa; and (e) its core income-generating activities are performed in Samoa. Failure to meet these conditions allows SIFA to revoke the tax exemption and reclassify the IC as a resident taxable company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa International Company to invoice bulk petrochemical trades while the actual management, sales negotiation, inventory control, and bank account operations all occur in a high-tax jurisdiction; creating a nominal Samoa office solely to claim tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act and Tax Administration Act, the Samoa Ministry of Revenue can disregard the IC's separate existence, assess the entity as a resident company at 27% on worldwide income, impose a 150% civil penalty on the tax avoided, and apply interest from the date the tax should have been paid. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion carries a fine of up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment for up to seven years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Samoan Registered Agent may be held jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax, penalties, and interest; the court may issue travel bans preventing departure from Samoa, order asset freezing, make directors personally liable for unlawful dividends, and disqualify directors from acting in Samoa for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC in legal form but with no employees, no bank account in Samoa, no records of board meetings in Samoa, and outsourcing all core functions to a service provider abroad; submitting a false economic substance self-declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFA will strike the company off the International Companies Register and revoke the tax exemption certificate under the Economic Substance Regulations; SIFA may levy a penalty of WST 200,000 and require the company to file and pay Samoan corporate income tax on its entire prior exempt income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false economic substance declarations are personally liable for fines up to WST 100,000; the court may order restitution to SIFA, compel production of personal tax records, and prohibit the director from being a director of any Samoan company for five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Compliance Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to process Swift LC and irrevocable LC payments for bulk petrochemical polymers while knowingly misrepresenting the beneficiary or end-user, submitting forged bills of lading, or structuring cash payments through Samoan banks below reporting thresholds to evade anti-money laundering screening.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 imposes a maximum penalty of WST 4,000,000 and imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering; Samoan correspondent banking relationships may be terminated, accounts frozen, and the IC dissolved for cause.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal criminal liability, confiscation of both Samoan and foreign assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act, travel bans, and extradition risk in jurisdictions with mutual legal assistance treaties with Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and retain Local File documentation, transfer pricing benchmarking, or economic substance evidence for related-party polymer procurement transactions above the WST 10,000,000 threshold; reporting a persistent operating margin below the arm's length net margin of comparable wholesale traders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Ministry of Revenue may make a transfer pricing adjustment reallocating additional taxable income to Samoa, impose a penalty equal to 25% of the adjustment amount, and add a monthly late payment penalty of WST 10,000 until compliant documentation is submitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing certificates or knowingly approve intercompany pricing without lawful economic support may be served Director Penalty Notices, rendering them personally liable for the adjusted tax debt; they may also be barred from serving as officers of a Samoan company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Return and Licence Fee
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC without filing the Annual Return or paying the SIFA licence fee for three successive years; continuing to open letters of credit and receive trade payments while the IC is suspended or struck off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic strike-off and dissolution under the International Companies Act; the IC loses legal capacity to hold assets, sue, or contract; bank accounts held in Samoa are frozen; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus WST 250 reinstatement fee and a late penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for debts incurred while the company is dissolved, and the Samoan Registered Agent may resign and notify SIFA, triggering immediate dissolution; courts may award restitution to creditors and prohibit the directors from forming any new Samoan company for up to five years.
